title: Heuristic Jam: Tooling Impressions & Backlog Sticky Notes
body:
Context:
This doc captures outputs from a 2-hour cross-functional "heuristic jam" (workshop + rapid review) run on 2026-06-09 and follow-up customer micro-interviews (6 participants) on 2026-06-12. Goal: surface quick wins and friction patterns in the Console + lightweight tooling flows (model selection, route creation, rollout config, cost estimates). Workshop attendees: product PMs, 2 UX researchers, 3 engineers from serving-runtime, 1 solutions engineer, 2 customer success reps.

Format & artifacts produced:
- 3 wireframe sketches per team area (model catalog, route builder, rollout page) pinned on Miro.
- 24 sticky-note usability observations clustered into 6 themes.
- Rapid affinity map and a lightweight prioritization (effort vs impact) done live.
- Follow-up 15-min moderated micro-interviews with current Dedicated and Hosted API power users; notes summarized below.

Top friction themes (synthesized):
1) Model discovery mismatch
   - Users expect example latency/cost at a glance; current catalog forces clicks to profile pages.
   - Confusion around model variants (quantized vs full-precision) — naming is inconsistent across flows.
   - Quote: "I want a one-line summary: latency @ 512 tokens, price per 1k, and recommended use cases."

2) Route builder cognitive load
   - Too many toggles in the route creation modal; users routinely miss the 'fallback' option.
   - The validation feedback is asynchronous and buried; users pressed Save then later discovered errors.
   - Participants tried to reuse previous routes but the copy flow copies deprecated flags.

3) Rollout visibility & rollback confidence
   - Users want a compact diff view comparing current vs proposed rollout rules.
   - Lack of live traffic estimate per variant (how many requests will hit this experiment) makes canary sizing guesswork.
   - Quote from SRE-oriented customer: "If I can't see expected hit percentage translated to expected QPS, I won't trust a canary."

4) Cost signal placement
   - Cost estimators are in a separate tab; users expect inline token cost projections when adjusting batching/seq len/quantization.
   - Embedding vs generation cost language is confusing for multi-mode routes.

5) Error & recovery paths
   - When a model fails fast (OOM/runtime), the platform surfaces a generic 500 with no guidance or suggested fallback.
   - Users want automatic fallback to a compatible smaller variant and a note explaining quality trade-offs.

6) Keyboard/power-user flows
   - Heavy-tabbers prefer compact tables and keyboard shortcuts; current console has many modal confirmations that break flow.

Wireframe writeups (high level notes):
- Model-list skimming row: add 3 inline columns: small badge for latency class (P0/P1), cost-per-1k-est., and a short tag-line (recommended-for: summarization, chat, embeddings). Clicking the badge expands a lightweight inline panel with a 30s perf/cost micro-summary rather than full model page.
- Route creation microflow: replace single big modal with stepper; step 1 = endpoints & mode, step 2 = model + variant selector with small cost preview, step 3 = traffic rules & fallback (with preview of estimated QPS). Add real-time validation and prevent Save if critical mismatch (warn inline).
- Rollout diff: small two-column diff widget showing "current" vs "proposed" with expected % traffic (configurable) and small risk indicator (low/medium/high) driven by historical error rates for model.

Backlog sticky notes -> groomed actions (ranked):
- A1 (high impact, low effort): Add inline cost-per-1k badge to model rows + tooltip micro-summary. (Jira: RI-1423)
- A2 (high impact, medium effort): Route builder stepper + real-time validation (split into backend validation API + frontend UX). Checkpoints: API contract by eng infra, frontend prototype in spike. (Jira: RI-1478, RI-1479)
- B1 (medium impact, medium effort): Rollout diff widget + expected QPS estimator (requires traffic-profile sampling from observability).
- B2 (medium impact, low effort): Improve OOM/error guidance with suggested fallback button (map to compatible variant) and link to recent logs/SRE contact.
- C1 (low impact, low effort): Add keyboard shortcut cheat-sheet for power-user pages; small UX prefs toggle to reduce confirmations.
- C2 (low impact, high effort): Rename model variant taxonomy + global mapping; requires rollout of naming migration and migration helpers.

Open questions & research follow-ups:
- How accurate are traffic estimates we can expose without complex sampling? (engineering spikes required)
- Do customers want cost projections at route-level or request-level? (ask in next CS sync; add survey in in-app banner)
- For fallback automation, what SLA/contract needs to exist to auto-fallback on production customers? Legal/regulatory implications for Private deployments.

Quick experiment proposals (30–60 day cycles):
- Experiment 1: Inline model row cost micro-summary A/B test with 50% of new accounts; measure route creation completion rate + model selection time.
- Experiment 2: Route stepper prototype tested with 10 beta customers (solutions-eng led) to collect time-to-first-success + error rate during setup.

Suggested owners & next steps (week 1):
- Product (Maya) to create PRD stub for A2, include acceptance criteria from workshop.
- Eng infra (Jonas) to scope validation API + sample endpoints for expected QPS estimator.
- UX research (Riya) to run quick follow-up survey and 4 additional moderated sessions focusing on cost language.
- Solutions Eng (Samira) to recruit 6 customers for the stepper prototype test and prepare success metrics.

Appendix: raw workshop notes (abridged)
- Sticky cluster: "Can't tell cost" x6; phrasing used by participants: 'opaque', 'tone-deaf to ops costs'.
- Sticky cluster: "Too many toggles" x4; participants defaulted to leaving toggles unchecked when unsure.
- Wireframe sketch: route stepper (hand-drawn) — attached in Miro board (see linked_artifacts).
- Short quotes: "Love that you show model family but need example outputs"; "Make canary rules expressible with a slider and numeric input".

Notes to self: keep deliverables lightweight, prioritize items that unblock new route adoption and reduce aborted setup flows. Aim to push A1 + A2 into next two sprints as a paired frontend+API effort.

End of doc.
